title: Cohort Conductor: Sequential AB Experiment Orchestrator with Shadowing and Auto-stop
creator: Ava Chen
description: Design and implement a production-ready experiment conductor that runs A/B tests and canary rollouts for model versions with cohort-aware exposure controls, shadow traffic support, and sequential statistical stopping. The conductor should integrate with Console for configuring experiments, expose guardrails for customer safety budgets, surface per-cohort dashboards, and provide automatic rollback triggers when quality or reliability regressions are detected.
background_and_motivation: Teams deploying new model variants need a unified way to run progressive exposure tests that respect latency and cost SLOs while detecting quality regressions early. Current ad-hoc scripts and manual traffic splits cause slow iterations and risk customer-facing incidents. We want an orchestration layer in the Console that codifies exposure budgets, cohort routing, and sequential hypothesis checks so teams can safely ship model upgrades.
goals: Ship an experiment conductor UI in Console to create and manage A/B and canary experiments
Support shadow traffic (one-way duplication) to gather internal metrics without exposing traffic
Implement exposure budgets by cohort with auto-throttle and manual override
Provide sequential statistical tests (e.g., alpha-spending) for early stopping and auto-rollback triggers
Instrument dashboards showing per-metric cohort deltas, sample sizes, and power estimates
non_goals: Building a generic offline AB engine for non-inference workloads
Replacing full experiment analysis pipelines used by research teams (we will export data for intensive analysis)
Implementing every statistical test initially; start with two robust options
acceptance_criteria: Console flow to create experiment with: baseline model, candidate model(s), cohorts, exposure schedule, shadow toggle
Runtime can route traffic splits and duplicate shadow requests to candidate models without affecting latency to end-users
Sequential stopping engine evaluates configured metrics every 10 minutes and can mark experiments as 'pause' or 'rollback' based on thresholds
Dashboards show p-values, effect sizes, and cumulative sample counts per cohort and per-route
Experiment REST API returns experiment status and recent decision history for automation and notifications
metrics_and_stat_checks: Primary metrics: quality_score (eval-based), error_rate (exceptions/invalid responses), latency_p95
Secondary metrics: cost_per_token, completion_rate, hallucination_rate (as detected by eval heuristics)
Sequential tests: alpha-spending (O'Brien-Fleming style) and Bayesian sequential comparison (posterior probability of improvement > 0.975)
Minimum sample per cohort before checks: configurable default 1,000 requests
Required uplift thresholds for promote: quality_score uplift >= 0.5% and no regression on latency_p95 > 10%
traffic_and_exposure_controls: Static split design (e.g., 95/5 canary) and ramp schedules (5% -> 20% -> 50% over configurable windows)
Cohort binding: support binding by user_id hashing, geo, workspace, or custom attribute
Shadow traffic mode duplicates requests to candidate model(s) asynchronously; responses are recorded but never returned to user
Exposure budget: token-based budget and request-count budget per cohort with automatic throttle to stay within budget
Burst-cap policy: allow short-lived spikes up to 2x configured exposure if operator allows
rollback_and_failure_modes: Auto-rollback triggers when any critical metric breaches configured safety thresholds for N consecutive evaluation windows
Rollback actions: revert traffic routing to last known-good model, mark experiment as 'rolled back', notify owners via configured channels
Graceful fallback: if candidate model fails at runtime (exceptions or OOM), route traffic to fallback model and mark experiment blocked
Manual override UI and API for operators to pause/resume or force-rollback experiments
observability_and_alerting: Per-experiment dashboard in Console: time-series for all tracked metrics, cohort comparisons, cumulative sample sizes
Automated alerts: send when p-value crosses configured thresholds, when latency_p95 regresses > 10%, or when shadow errors exceed baseline by X
Audit logs for routing decisions, exposure throttle events, and auto-rollback actions
Export hooks: clickstream and raw model responses available in S3/BigQuery for offline analysis
console_ui_wireframe_notes: Experiment creation page: step 1 select baseline and candidate models (from model catalog), step 2 select cohorts and exposure schedule, step 3 choose stats config and primary/secondary metrics, step 4 safety budgets and alert contacts. Include a preview of routing rules and estimated QPS + token exposure. Persistent experiment timeline view with decision markers.
api_contracts: POST /experiments to create with JSON payload describing cohorts, splits, metrics, and safety policies
GET /experiments/{id}/status returns state, last_decision, samples_collected, metric_summaries
PUT /experiments/{id}/pause or /resume and /rollback for operator controls
Webhook endpoints: experiment.decision and experiment.alert to be consumed by PagerDuty/Slack integrations
integration_points: Model Catalog for selecting versions and compatible fallback variants
Serving Router for traffic splits and shadow duplication
Optimize recommendations to suggest quantization or smaller variants when cost budgets are hit
Console dashboards and Alerting backend for notifications
Telemetry pipeline (metrics + traces) for feeding sequential tests
implementation_phases: Phase 1 (MVP): basic split routing + shadowing + simple sequential alpha-spending check + Console create/get APIs
Phase 2: cohort binding rules, exposure budgets, improved UI, and automatic rollback hooks
Phase 3: Bayesian sequential engine, multi-metric composite tests, adaptive ramping based on signal strength
Phase 4: tenant-level guardrails, enterprise controls (approval workflows, audit retention)
open_questions: Which default statistical engine do we enable for new experiments? alpha-spending or Bayesian?
What is the correct default minimum sample size for generative quality signals given heavy variance?
How do we reliably compute a real-time quality_score for chat completions without human labels? (we have heuristics but accuracy needs validation)
Should shadow traffic sampling be CDC-based (percentage of requests) or triggered by deterministic cohorts only?
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: false positives from noisy quality signals leading to unnecessary rollbacks -> Mitigation: require multi-window confirmation and multiple metrics before rollback
Risk: shadowing significantly increases cost -> Mitigation: cap shadow sampling rate and provide cost estimator in Console
Risk: routing bugs causing customer exposure -> Mitigation: extensive unit/integration tests, staged rollout of conductor itself, and kill-switch per workspace
